issues.legal_issue: The meaning and validity of legislation cannot be controlled by its statement of objects and reasons or by changing executive policy when the enacted words point otherwise.
material_facts: The legislation provided for control and regulation of trade in specified forest produce through a State monopoly.
The challengers relied on the legislation’s statement of objects and reasons and the State’s industrial policy to argue that the law and notification served only to prevent smuggling.
The Court considered the enacted provisions and the preamble in deciding the legislation’s object and scope.
issues.conclusion: The legislation’s object included creating a State monopoly, and its meaning and the validity of the notification could not be determined merely by the statement of objects and reasons or changing government policy.
issues.legal_principle: The preamble may assist in understanding an enactment, but a statement of objects and reasons cannot control the meaning of its substantive provisions or cut down the generality of their words. Executive policy likewise cannot control the enacted text. The Court relied on Central Bank of India v. Their Workmen, [1960] 1 SCR 200, and State of West Bengal v. Union of India, [1964] 1 SCR 371.

rule.if: statutory_interpretation_dispute and (explanatory_material_is_invoked or executive_policy_is_invoked) and enacted_words_address_the_subject

predicates.statutory_interpretation_dispute: The proceeding requires the court to determine the meaning or application of legislation.
predicates.explanatory_material_is_invoked: A party relies on a statement explaining the legislation’s objects or reasons to support its proposed interpretation.
predicates.executive_policy_is_invoked: A party relies on the government’s policy to support its proposed interpretation.
predicates.enacted_words_address_the_subject: The legislation’s enacted provisions address the subject in dispute.

issues.definition: When a statutory interpretation dispute turns on enacted provisions addressing the subject, those words govern even if explanatory material or executive policy is invoked.

issues.legal_issue: A law creating a State monopoly in trade may impose restrictions that are presumed reasonable and in the interest of the general public.
material_facts: The law placed trade in specified forest produce under a State monopoly.
The challengers argued that the annulment of their contracts and restrictions on their trading rights were unreasonable or arbitrary.
issues.conclusion: The restrictions were to be presumed reasonable and in the interest of the general public; the State could create a partial or complete monopoly in trade.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(6)(ii) permits laws relating to State monopolies, and a law governing such trading activity is presumed reasonable and in the interest of the general public. The Court relied on Akadasi Padhan v. State of Orissa, [1963] 2 Supp. SCR 691.

predicates.state_monopoly_restriction_challenge: The proceeding challenges restrictions imposed in connection with a State monopoly in trade.
predicates.law_places_trade_under_state_monopoly: The law places the relevant trade under a partial or complete State monopoly.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns restrictions connected with a law placing trade under a State monopoly, the restrictions are presumed reasonable and in the general public interest.

issues.legal_issue: The legislature may retrospectively change the legal basis of a judicial decision and thereby make it ineffective, but may not set it aside by a bare declaration.
material_facts: An earlier judgment held that the former statutory provisions did not cover forest produce grown in Government forests.
The later ordinance enlarged the definition of forest produce and amended the provision rescinding contracts to cover produce grown or found on Government land and in Government forests.
The amendments were given retrospective effect, and the challengers argued that the ordinance encroached on judicial power by nullifying the earlier judgment.
issues.conclusion: The ordinance validly removed the statutory basis for the earlier decision and did not encroach on judicial power; retrospective legislation was permissible subject to legislative competence and other constitutional limits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 245 and 246, the legislature may enact valid retrospective legislation and render a judicial decision ineffective by changing the legal basis on which it rested. Validating legislation that removes the cause of invalidity or ineffectiveness is not an encroachment on judicial power, but a bare legislative declaration cannot directly overrule or set aside a judicial decision. The Court relied on Hari Singh v. The Military Estate Officer, [1973] 1 SCR 515; Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Hindustan Tools Ltd., [1975] Supp. SCR 394; V.N. Saxena v. State of M.P., [1976] 3 SCR 237; and Misri Lal Jain v. State of Orissa, [1977] 3 SCR 714.

rule.if: validating_legislation_challenge and earlier_judgment_rest_on_old_legal_basis and later_law_changes_that_basis and later_law_is_within_legislative_competence and later_law_does_more_than_declare_the_judgment_wrong

predicates.validating_legislation_challenge: The proceeding challenges legislation enacted to validate action affected by an earlier judicial decision.
predicates.earlier_judgment_rest_on_old_legal_basis: The earlier judgment rested on the scope or effect of the law as it stood before the later enactment.
predicates.later_law_changes_that_basis: The later enactment changes the legal provisions that formed the basis of the earlier judgment.
predicates.later_law_is_within_legislative_competen: The later enactment is within the legislature’s authority and is not barred by another constitutional limitation.
predicates.later_law_does_more_than_declare_the_jud: The later enactment changes the governing law rather than merely declaring the earlier judgment to be wrong.

issues.definition: A validating enactment may make an earlier judgment ineffective without judicial encroachment when it changes the legal basis of the judgment, is within legislative competence, and does more than declare the judgment wrong.

issues.legal_issue: A validating enactment may make an existing notification effective for produce newly brought within the statute without requiring a fresh notification.
material_facts: An existing notification brought the statute into force in the whole State in relation to sal seeds.
The ordinance amended the statutory definition and contract-rescission provisions to include produce grown or found on State-owned land and in Government forests.
The ordinance expressly validated the existing notification as covering sal seeds grown or found on those lands and forests.
The State had not issued a fresh notification after the amendments.
issues.conclusion: The existing notification was valid and effective for sal seeds grown or found in Government forests, and no fresh notification was required to cover the contracts in question.
issues.legal_principle: The ordinance amended the definition of forest produce and the provision governing rescission of contracts, gave those amendments retrospective effect, and expressly validated the existing notification notwithstanding contrary judicial decisions. The Court held that the notification was effective as if issued under the amended law. It relied on the amended provisions corresponding to sections 2(c), 5(1)(a), and the ordinance’s validation provision.

predicates.challenge_to_validated_notification: The proceeding challenges whether an existing notification remains effective after legislation is amended to validate it.
predicates.existing_notification_identifies_the_rel: The existing notification identifies the kind of produce to which the statutory scheme applies.
predicates.amended_law_covers_produce_on_state_land: The amended law includes the relevant produce when grown or found on State-owned land or in Government forests.
predicates.validation_expressly_extends_the_notific: The validating enactment expressly treats the existing notification as applying to the newly covered produce.

issues.definition: When an existing notification identifies the relevant produce and a validating enactment expressly extends it to produce newly covered on State land, the notification is effective without a fresh notification.

issues.legal_issue: A State carrying on a monopoly trade cannot use private contractors or agents to conduct that trade for their own benefit rather than on the State’s behalf.
material_facts: The legislation established a State monopoly in specified forest produce.
The challengers contended that the law did not bar future contracts like their existing collection contracts.
The Court stated that State parties or agents employed in the trade must work on behalf of the State and not for themselves.
issues.conclusion: It would be impermissible for the State to enter into future contracts of the kind in which private parties conduct the monopoly trade for their own benefit.
issues.legal_principle: When the State conducts trade, it may act through its officers or agents, but agents must carry on the trade on behalf of the State rather than for themselves. The Court relied on Akadasi Padhan v. State of Orissa, [1963] 2 Supp. SCR 691.

predicates.state_monopoly_trade: The State conducts or is entitled to conduct the relevant trade under a monopoly.
predicates.proposed_private_contracts_allow_agents_: Proposed contracts would allow private parties or agents to conduct the monopoly trade for their own benefit rather than on the State’s behalf.

issues.definition: When trade is conducted under a State monopoly, contracts allowing private parties or agents to trade for their own benefit are impermissible.
